A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 44-page versions of Learnable Kernel Density Estimation for Graphs. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish matching research content throughout the main text and appendices.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A report original synthetic graph density-estimation experiments, graph anomaly-detection benchmarks, ablations and contamination analyses.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A retain the same original experimental results, including synthetic density estimation and graph anomaly detection.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendices C–D retain identical graph representations, MMD computation, multi-scale KDE, perturbations, training objective and inference procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic Erdős–Rényi graph density estimation and anomaly detection on the same eleven TU datasets, including the same training-contamination scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches in Tables 1, 5, 6 and 8: PK/WL with SVM or iForest, the six GNN baselines, and the supplementary InfoGraph+KDE and GAE+KDE comparisons.

E3.justification: Synthetic-data generation, sample counts, class-based anomaly settings, AUROC/AUPRC/FPR95 metrics and training configurations remain identical in Section 5 and Appendix F.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendices A and C retain the same component ablations, bandwidth and depth analyses, contamination experiments, density visualizations and spectral-perturbation case studies.

E5.justification: Both report five trials with different random seeds and identical uncertainty-reporting practices, including mean and standard deviation in Table 2 and the experimental details in Appendix F.4.

E6.justification: Numerical results and graphical findings are identical, including all appendix results. LGKDE's reported average AUROC, AUPRC and FPR95 remain 78.57%, 87.69% and 61.62% in Tables 1, 5 and 6.

T1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E retain identical definitions, assumptions, consistency and convergence guarantees, robustness bounds, complexity analyses and proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list and conclusion are unchanged, retaining the same methodological contributions, theoretical guarantees and claimed empirical advantages.

C2.justification: Interpretations of learned densities, joint optimization and contamination robustness are unchanged. Page 44 retains the same limitations concerning quadratic scaling and extensions beyond undirected homogeneous graphs.

D1.justification: Appendices C, D and F retain identical pseudocode, hyperparameters, RTX 4090 hardware information and Listing 1. Both versions state that code will become public after acceptance.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix B and the reference list are identical. Neither cited works nor positioning relative to previous graph-density and anomaly-detection research changes.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1, dated 27 May 2025, to v2, dated 20 August 2025. The paper's wording, headings, terminology and section order are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: The updated first-page arXiv margin stamp has a slight positional adjustment. Figures 1–12, Tables 1–9, algorithms, captions and all remaining page layouts are visually identical.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, results, proofs, implementation disclosures and limitations are identical across both complete PDFs. Updates to the arXiv stamp and PDF metadata do not meaningfully affect the paper's evidence, clarity or overall quality.
